title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (ACME CFI-G)
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-159: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G). https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-159
objectives: Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane in normal and inverse spherical diffusion flame configurations aboard the ISS.
approach: Perform spherical diffusion flame tests in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) across variable reactant dilutions, pressures, and oxygen concentrations up to 85% O2 creating inside-out inverted flames.

title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design (ACME/Flame Design)
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-10: ACME / Flame Design. https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-10
objectives: Obtain soot-inception limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames as functions of flow rate, stoichiometric mixture fraction (Zst), and inert (N2/CO2) dilution.
approach: Perform spherical diffusion flame tests in drop towers and aboard the ISS using the modular ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR).

title: ACME Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (E-FIELD Flames)
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-22: ACME E-FIELD Flames. https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo
objectives: Evaluate the influence of electric fields on flame ions to control flame stability, soot formation, and mimic partial-gravity buoyancy regimes.
approach: Apply controlled DC/AC electric fields across laminar gaseous diffusion flames in CIR-ACME to emulate partial-gravity conditions relevant to Lunar (1/6g) and Martian (3/8g) habitats prior to LUCI and FM2.

title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II)
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-26: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II). https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-26
objectives: Determine flammability limits, flame spread rates, and nitrogen extinguishment thresholds for solid spacecraft fabrics and plastics under low-speed forced airflow.
approach: Burn solid samples (cotton-fiberglass SIBAL, PMMA, Nomex) inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) using the fan-driven SPICE flow duct at oxygen concentrations up to 35%.

title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2)
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-142: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2). https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-142
objectives: Quantify minimum CO2 and Helium diluent concentrations required to extinguish spherical liquid fuel droplet flames and characterize dual-stage cool flame extinction.
approach: Deploy and ignite single and dual liquid hydrocarbon droplets (heptane, methanol, octane) inside the Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) within the CIR.

title: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Analysis
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-117: CFD Analysis of Cool Flame Dynamics using FLEX Data. https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-117
objectives: Use flight data obtained from PSI through NASA's Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) to quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations affect cool flame dynamics.
approach: Develop a 3-D OpenFOAM CFD model of n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity, coupling variable-density Navier-Stokes flow with low-temperature combustion chemistry.

title: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment (SPICE)
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-107: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment (SPICE). https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-107
objectives: Measure laminar jet diffusion flame smoke points and soot inception limits in microgravity under controlled co-flow ventilation.
approach: Burn gaseous ethylene and methane jets inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) using the modular fan-driven SPICE flow duct and compare with 1g terrestrial smoke points.

title: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Investigation PSI-60: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets. https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-60
objectives: Increase understanding of the mechanisms controlling the large discrepancy between soot formation in 1g and 0g flames by extracting soot volume fractions from SPICE imagery.
approach: Combine color-ratio pyrometry post-processing of SPICE flight imagery with detailed soot modeling to bound 0g vs. 1g particulate emission.

title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration (Saffire-I, -II, and -III)
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration (Saffire-I, -II, and -III). https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo
objectives: Investigate realistic large-scale flame growth, material flammability, and smoke/gas dispersion inside an uncrewed spacecraft cabin.
approach: Ignite large fabric and polymer panels inside an uncrewed Cygnus resupply vehicle after ISS departure across variable oxygen and cabin ventilation regimes.

title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME / SAME-R) & DAFT
doi_citation: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME / SAME-R) and Dust Feasibility Test (DAFT). https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo
objectives: Measure smoke particle size distributions from overheated spacecraft materials in microgravity to improve smoke detector reliability and prevent false alarms.
approach: Analyze smoke aerosols generated by smoldering wire insulation and polymers in the CIR, cross-referenced with DAFT/DAFT-2 dust detection instrumentation.
